annotation.interpretation_a: Implementations can use *any* normalization method they choose, even proprietary ones, as long as equivalent URIs are treated as the same resource.
annotation.interpretation_b: Implementations *should* use a standard normalization method (like the one in Section 6.2 of [URI]), but are permitted to use others. The phrase 'using any method' implies a broad range of acceptable methods, but doesn't explicitly require adherence to a standard.
annotation.justification: The phrase 'using any method' is underspecified. It doesn't state whether implementations must adhere to a standard normalization method or if they can use any arbitrary method. This creates ambiguity in how URIs are normalized and compared, potentially leading to interoperability issues.
annotation.missing_information: It is unclear whether 'any method' implies that implementations are free to choose any normalization algorithm, or if there is an expectation of interoperability through a common standard. A constraint on the normalization method would resolve the ambiguity.
